description: Authz recogniser corpus (BACKLOG CN-06). Each case is scanned as its own root with --authz --multiagent. Positives name the file, line and rule that must be reported; negatives must produce no finding for the listed rules at all. Seeded from AZ-03 through AZ-12; every case that was wrong on 2026-09-19 is labelled with its item.

scoring.hit: every (file, line, rule) in `expect` is reported
scoring.clean: none of `rules` is reported anywhere in the case
scoring.gates: recall on expected=detect must be 1.0 and false positives on expected=clean must be 0

cases.description: Flask app whose only principal is session['user_id']; the pass must switch on and report the unguarded read.
The same read guarded against session['user_id'].
Flask-Login's documented current_user.get_id() compared to str(doc.owner_id).
DRF ViewSet retrieve() reading by pk with no object check; list() is scoped and must not be reported.
Django CBV reading Document.objects.get(pk=kwargs['pk']); the scoped twin must not be reported.
APIView calling self.check_object_permissions(request, doc), and one comparing doc.owner to request.user.
A login handler reading User by request.form['email'] has no object to own.
filter_by(owner=current_user).all() is scoped; Tag.query.all() is a lookup table.
Document is written with owner_id=current_user.id elsewhere and read with Document.query.all() in an authenticated handler.
A helper whose first parameter is named request is not a route handler.
The admin-override shape the rule's own remediation recommends.
Caller-supplied owner with no guard at all.
A fail-closed same-module superuser helper dominates two user-keyed reads.
CrewAI t1(scrape) -> t2(writer) -> t3(code exec): two hops.
doc.owner.equals(req.user._id) and doc.owner.toString() !== req.user.id are owner guards.
app.get('/f/:id', auth, getDoc) with getDoc declared as a named function; the inline guarded handler must not be reported.
app.route('/g/:id').get(auth, handler) with an unguarded inline handler.
